newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev deposit rates fall in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev deposit rates fall in thin trade.

text.p: The interbank deposit rates fell in thin trade on the money market in line with a main interest rate cut which came into force on Monday, dealers said.
"Banks prefer to regulate their liquidity by selling treasury paper directly instead of bidding for funds on the interbank deposit market," said dealer.
Traders said that banks' liquidity was high which reflected in low demand for government securities on the secondary market.
The central bank cut its simple annual main rate to 6.96 percent from 9.76 percent, effective from July 14.

Prime minister Ivan Kostov said in a state radio interview on Monday that the falling lev rates showed the currency board system was working and urged banks to lend credits to enterprising businessmen.
Banks' liquidity improved after a currency board launch on July 1 after they sold marks purchased earlier at lower rates.
The central bank was buying marks 995 levs and selling at 1,000 after a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 levs per mark was introduced.
Overnight interbank depo rates eased to 3.0-4.0 percent annually from 4.0-4.5 percent on Friday. Spot week rates were around 4.5-5.0 percent against 5.0-5.5 percent.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 4.80 percent on Friday against 4.83 percent on Thursday, a central bank official said.
